lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. Amy gets a dimmer.
lines.script: [busy, cheerful] Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. Amy gets a dimmer.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. Also, why are you sticky?
lines.script: [warm] Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. Also, why are you sticky?

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. Before lunch.
lines.script: [casual brag] Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. Before lunch.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. I got a truck and two girls. Living the song.
lines.script: [easy, amused] Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. I got a truck and two girls. Living the song.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. It was a playoff game. We lost.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. It was a playoff game. We lost.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. And I built that deck.
lines.script: [soft, sincere] Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. And I built that deck.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. So I came back too. I brought bread.
lines.script: [cheerful, relieved] Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. So I came back too. I brought bread.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Take some for the road. Don't tell Gary.
lines.script: [generous] Take some for the road. Don't tell Gary.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Every conference night. Twelve years. It's the only reason Gary shows up.
lines.script: [easygoing, warm] Every conference night. Twelve years. It's the only reason Gary shows up.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: It's store-bought.
lines.script: [flat confession, guilty] It's store-bought.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [satisfied] The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: It lights up. Every letter. I'm an electrician, Gracie. It was never going to just hang there.
lines.script: [proud] It lights up. Every letter. I'm an electrician, Gracie. It was never going to just hang there.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Hold this. No, the other end. It's the OTHER banner. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [impatient] Hold this. No, the other end. It's the OTHER banner. Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Conference night is over. I survived. I'm going to sit on this couch until Field Day.
lines.script: [slumping] Conference night is over. I survived. I'm going to sit on this couch until Field Day.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Deedee’s plate? Oh, everybody waits for Deedee’s plate. She brings one every conference night.
lines.script: [reverent] Deedee’s plate? Oh, everybody waits for Deedee’s plate. She brings one every conference night.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Don't tell Gary. Gary eats the whole thing.
lines.script: [conspiratorial, whispering] Don't tell Gary. Gary eats the whole thing.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. That's allowed. It's in the contract.
lines.script: [low, hiding] Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. That's allowed. It's in the contract.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: If you're hungry, the fridge is a minefield. Every lunch in there has a name on it. Read the labels.
lines.script: [warning, deadpan] If you're hungry, the fridge is a minefield. Every lunch in there has a name on it. Read the labels.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [quick warning] Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? Both. Correct. Go get 'em.
lines.script: Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? Both. Correct. Go get 'em.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Long Island born. Country music raised. Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Long Island born. Country music raised. Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Big game tonight. If you hear yelling, that's me. If you hear crying, that's also me.
lines.script: [hyped] Big game tonight. If you hear yelling, that's me. If you hear crying, that's also me.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. I know. It's on the list.
lines.script: [calm heads-up, then sheepish] Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. I know. It's on the list.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.
lines.script: [easygoing, eager] Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.
lines.script: [warm, cheerful] Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.
lines.script: [easygoing, dry] No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
lines.script: [relaxed, amused] Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
